title: Gate in the unrolled circuit
statement: Let $M$ be a sequential Boolean circuit with $n$ inputs and $r$ registers, and let $p$ be a nonnegative integer. Write $s$ for the circuit size, $q=\lfloor p/s\rfloor$ for the block number, and $j=p\bmod s$ for the position within the block. If $j<r$ and $q=0$, the gate is an argument-free AND gate when register $j$ is initially true and an argument-free OR gate otherwise; if $j<r$ and $q>0$, it is an AND gate whose sole argument is the vertex for register $j$'s next value placed in block $q-1$. If $j\ge r$, take the combinational gate at index $j-r$ (using an argument-free AND gate if that index is out of range); the resulting gate has that gate's kind and its arguments placed in block $q$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a sequential circuit with $n$ inputs and $r$ registers
